tagline.text: A white sandbar off Panglao that appears only at low tide

location.label: Location
location.text: Off the southwest coast of Panglao Island, Bohol (around Pungtud Island)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: February–May dry season, morning low tide

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day (as part of an island hopping tour)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱900–2,500 (per person on a shared island hopping boat; entrance and environmental fees extra with some operators)

children.text: Virgin Island is a white sandbar off Panglao Island in Bohol that emerges only at low tide; locally it is called Pungtud Island. It is a 20–30 minute boat ride from Alona Beach and is most often visited as the last stop of an island hopping tour that also includes Balicasag Island and dolphin watching.

Virgin Island is a small uninhabited sand islet floating in the sea off the southwest of Panglao Island, Bohol. Maps label it Pungtud (or Puntod) Island, and it is also known by the Italian-style name Isola di Francesco. When the water drops, a long strip of white sand appears in the middle of the blue sea, and when the tide comes in it mostly disappears underwater. So the same spot looks completely different depending on when you arrive.

You do not stay overnight here or visit it on its own; it is one stop on a Panglao island hopping tour. A common itinerary among Korean travelers is to leave Alona Beach early in the morning, watch dolphins, snorkel at Balicasag Island, and then stop at Virgin Island around midday to walk on the sandbar. It is close to Panglao Island, so the boat ride takes only about
20–30 minutes

There is some news worth knowing. The island was closed around September 2024 because of coral damage and waste problems, and it reopened in early February 2026 under the leadership of the Bohol provincial government. With the reopening came new rules such as a cap on visitor numbers, a mandatory environmental briefing, and a ban on vendors, and the detailed guidelines are still being refined. Fees, vendors, and ways of staying described in older reviews may differ from today, so check with your tour operator and the latest announcements before you leave. The name can also be confusing. There are several islands called Virgin Island in the Philippines, and the one in this guide is the sandbar off Panglao in Bohol. Local tour apps and maps sometimes label it Pungtud Island or Isola di Francesco, so when you book it is safest to specify "Panglao Virgin Island." According to OpenStreetMap it lies around latitude 9.56 and longitude 123.72, in the sea west of Alona Beach.

To be honest, the sandbar itself is a modest place where you mostly walk around and take a few photos. Even so, the scenery of shallow emerald water, white sand, and the Panglao coastline in the distance has become one of the signature photos of a Bohol trip. It is best enjoyed as one easy closing stop of an island hopping tour rather than with big expectations.

blocks.title: A white sandbar that opens only at low tide

children.text: When the water drops, a path of sand appears in the middle of the sea, and you can walk over clear, ankle-deep water. The size and shape of the sand keep changing with that day's tide.
The shallow water looks a bright turquoise, with the Panglao coastline in the background. The water color is clearest in the late morning when the sun is high.

blocks.title: The finale of an island hopping tour

children.text: On shared tours departing from Alona Beach, the usual order is dolphin watching, snorkeling at Balicasag Island, and then a stop here. The travel time is short, so the day is not overly tiring.

blocks.title: Shallow coral waters around Pungtud Island

children.text: The reopening rules set time limits on snorkeling and diving, separate from sandbar visits. Activities are led by accredited guides and supervised by the Protected Area Management Office.

blocks.title: Management that changed with the reopening

children.text: Registration and an environmental briefing are required before landing, and boats come and go through a single designated point. You can expect a calmer and cleaner atmosphere than before.

blocks.title: Combine it with Balicasag Island and dolphin watching

children.text: Combining early-morning dolphin watching, turtle and coral snorkeling at Balicasag, and Virgin Island on one boat lets you enjoy the most popular Bohol sea stops in a single day.

The boat heads out to sea to look for dolphins. Be sure to check whether the dolphin watching fee and permit are included in the base tour price.
Arrive at Balicasag Island and snorkel. The marine sanctuary environmental fee is often paid separately on arrival.
Arrive at Virgin Island. If the tide is right, the sandbar is widely exposed; after registering and attending the environmental briefing, walk the sandbar and take photos.

These times are an example of a shared tour from one review article and vary by operator and tide. Ask the operator you booked with for the confirmed schedule.

items.subtitle: A relaxed schedule built around the tide

children.text: With a private boat you can set the departure time yourself according to the tide table. First ask the operator when the sandbar is most widely exposed.
Leave Alona Beach and arrive at Pungtud Island about
20–30 minutes
later. Complete registration, the environmental briefing, and payment of fees.
Walk the sandbar and take photos, then, if you have time, snorkel with an accredited guide. Activities must finish within
2 hours
at most.
Move on toward Balicasag Island or return to Alona Beach for lunch. A private boat is more relaxed if you cut down the number of stops.
See the cost table below for private boat prices. It is said that with four or more people, the cost per person is often similar to or lower than a shared tour.
There are direct flights from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). The airport opened in November 2018 to replace Tagbilaran Airport, and flights to and from Manila are frequent.
The flight takes a little over an hour; check the latest information for each airline's schedule by season.
From Panglao Airport to Alona Beach takes about
20–50 minutes
You can also connect through Cebu. The fast ferry from Cebu to Tagbilaran takes under 2 hours.

Since the reopening, all tourist boats must use Pungtud Island as the single designated entry and exit point, so boats cannot land elsewhere on their own.
Landing may change depending on the tide, the weather, and visitor limits.

For Virgin Island, the tide matters more than the season. The sandbar appears only at low tide, so even on a beautiful day you will see almost nothing at high tide. Check the tide table before booking and plan with your operator to arrive when the sandbar is most widely exposed.

In terms of season, the calmer dry season is more comfortable. However, one travel article warns that typhoon exposure is highest from roughly October to January, so extra schedule buffer and travel insurance are recommended in that period.

The most convenient place to stay is around Alona Beach, the departure point for island hopping tours. Many departures are very early in the morning, so staying near the pier makes the morning much easier. Besides Alona, Panglao Island also has many places to stay around Doljo Beach, in a range of price levels.

With the reopening, vendors are permanently banned on the island, so you are unlikely to meet the boats selling sea urchins or grilled seafood as in the past. Bring snacks and water in advance, and check whether lunch is included in the tour, otherwise eat at a restaurant in Alona Beach.

In the evening you can choose from the restaurants lined up along the Alona Beach road, serving grilled seafood and Filipino home cooking. On days with an early morning tour, it is better to cut down on late-night drinking the evening before. On Panglao Island you can get around even to farther places by tricycle or Grab, so on afternoons without hopping it is nice to stroll around the beaches and cafes.
Check the tide table before booking, and ask the operator when the sandbar is most widely exposed.
Shared tours often depart early in the morning and are frequently combined with dolphin watching. Bring seasickness medicine.
Be sure to ask what is included in the price. Entrance and environmental fees and the dolphin watching permit are often not part of the base price.
Use mineral-based sunscreen without oxybenzone or octinoxate, which are harmful to coral.
Prepare plenty of small bills. Many fees are paid in cash on site.
Group photos have a time limit, so take them quickly following your guide's instructions.
Some parts may be muddy, so sandals or water shoes that you do not mind getting wet are a good idea.
The day before your visit, confirm the meeting time, the tide, and possible weather changes with the operator by message so that you are not scrambling at dawn.
A wide-brimmed hat and a long-sleeved rash guard are useful on the sandbar. There is almost no shade, so the midday sun is strong.

This island was closed around September 2024 because of environmental problems and reopened in early February 2026, and the rules are still being refined. Be sure to check the latest announcements and your operator's guidance before visiting.
Landings are limited to 250 visitors every 2 hours, and snorkeling and diving are limited to a maximum of 2 hours. In peak season, landing may be delayed.
Do not step on or touch the coral, and do not leave marine life such as starfish you may come across lying out on the sand. Feeding marine animals is prohibited.
Throwing trash into the sea or burning it is prohibited. Trash is inspected before and after entry, so you must take back everything you brought.
When the tide comes in, the sandbar shrinks quickly, so keep to the boat's departure time. Landing may be cancelled in bad weather.

The entrance fee differs by source: about ₱100 for foreigners (₱30 for locals) in February 2026 reopening reports, and ₱200 from some operators. To avoid being overcharged, ask for the official fee schedule at the registration desk.
A marine sanctuary about
45 minutes
away by boat, and the classic stop combined with Virgin Island on island hopping tours. Snorkeling with turtles and coral is popular.
The departure point for island hopping tours and Panglao's signature beach, with accommodation and restaurants all in one place.
The whole island with the airport, beaches, and dive sites. Virgin Island lies in the sea off the southwest of this island.
